rung_2b_working_ladder_EXACT.method: Mojeek exact-phrase search-result pages retrieved through mcp__claude_ai_Exa__web_fetch_exa used purely as a FETCH TRANSPORT.
rung_2b_working_ladder_EXACT.why_this_is_exact_not_semantic: The query string, the quoting semantics, the matching and the ranking are all Mojeek's. Exa only retrieves the rendered results page. Mojeek honours double quotes strictly and reports the exact-match count explicitly, printing 'There were no exact matches for "X"' before falling back to unquoted results. These results are therefore EXACT-PHRASE evidence, not semantic.
controls_run: "Sixten Sason" -> 'Results 1 to 10 from 1,033' (known real Swedish industrial designer) - index is live and substantive
"Jonas Malmryd" -> 'Results 1 to 4 from 4' then 'There were no more results for "Jonas Malmryd"' - quoting is strict and the known prior Malmryd finding reproduces
rung_2b_working_ladder_EXACT.index_caveat: Mojeek is an independent crawler with a smaller index than Google. A zero on Mojeek is weaker evidence than a zero on Google, and its Swedish-language coverage is thinner than its English coverage. Zeros below should be read as 'no exact bearer in an independent full-text index', not as proof of universal non-existence.
rung_2b_working_ladder_EXACT.operational_notes: Batching more than ~2 Mojeek URLs per Exa fetch triggers CRAWL_UNKNOWN_ERROR / CRAWL_LIVECRAWL_TIMEOUT or a Mojeek captcha. Adding a throwaway '&reg=&t=N' parameter reliably busted cached error states. Boolean OR in the query string reliably triggered the captcha and was avoided.

entries.collision_reasoning: The fictional entity is bylined '- Verity Padgham, weekend columnist'. Mike Padgham's Yorkshire Post pieces carry the identical structural signature: a regional-newspaper opinion column, filed under 'columnists', bylined '- Mike Padgham'. That is a real bearer in the byline's own field. Two independent reasons this is actionable rather than a judgement call: (1) the unit's shipped originality_note asserts 'critically for a byline, no journalist or columnist named Padgham in the results' - exact-phrase search falsifies that assertion, so a factual claim in shipped generator_meta is wrong; (2) the SAME unit rejected the candidate name 'Verity Ashlock' on precisely this ground, recording 'two real journalists bear the surname Ashlock ... i.e. a real bearer in the byline's own field'. Applying that stated standard consistently, Padgham should have been rejected too. Counter-argument the orchestrator should weigh: Mike Padgham's primary identity is care-sector chair rather than professional journalist, he writes op-eds rather than staffing a column, and the full name 'Verity Padgham' has zero bearers. entries.orchestrator_note: BORDERLINE - escalatable to COLLISION at orchestrator discretion. The unit is set squarely in Swedish kommunal förvaltning (a kommunrevision audit of sports-hall bookings), and a real Steneryd sits in Swedish local government. Graded RECORDED rather than COLLISION for three reasons: (1) the real bearer is a förtroendevald (elected politician) while the fictional Tora Steneryd is a tjänsteman (employed leisure officer) - a distinction this very passage turns on; (2) no bearer exists in leisure or sport administration, the fictional character's actual function; (3) Steneryd is a genuine Swedish village name, so it arises naturally as a toponymic surname rather than reading as a borrowed identity. NOTE: the unit's originality_note asserts the Steneryd bearers lie 'i obesläktade fält', citing only a 1964 maths teacher and the Torhamn village name. entries.name: Rimhall
queries: "Rimhall" surname person Utah pioneer or city directory historical record (Exa - SEMANTIC, re-examination of prior finding)

'"Rimhall" surname genealogy' returned 0. SEMANTIC re-examination of the prior US finding confirms it: 'RIMHALL, GEORGE HENRY' and 'RIMHALL, GEORGE WASHINGTON' in 'Pioneers and prominent men of Utah'; 'Rimhall Jack r109 Phillips cir' in Hill's Charlotte (Mecklenburg County, N.C.) City Directory 1962; 'J. E. RIMHALL' in an 1875 Chicago Tribune classified; 'Rimhall Street' in a US city directory.
entries.orchestrator_note: Two independent reasons this is not a kill. First, domain: 19th-century Utah settlers, a 1962 Charlotte resident and an 1875 Chicago advertiser are as far from modern Swedish ethnology as a bearer can get. Second, provenance: these are very likely OCR corruptions of Brimhall/Bramhall, not genuine Rimhalls - the BYU Utah Supreme Court brief in the same result set renders 'BRIMHALL' as 'RIMHALL' in its own OCR layer within a single document, and the Utah pioneer listing sits inside a documented Bramhall-Brimhall family record. The prior finding is upheld as accurate but harmless.

No national trade register, Companies House, Ordnance Survey gazetteer or Swedish Lantmäteriet gazetteer was queried directly - only open-web exact-phrase search.
